title: The fan, made precise
question: You picked the fan and said it is still very imprecise. It is: the arc opened 178 degrees, so the two end discs sat level with the hub and the shape read as a horseshoe - and the discs floated on nothing, with no line for the eye to check them against. Three answers.

options.label: A · a groove
options.thesis: A channel pressed into the ground along the arc, with the discs sitting in it - the tube vocabulary at arc scale. The arc is 150 degrees now, so every disc is visibly above the hub.
options.viewport: Eight discs seated in a groove around the hub.
options.risk: The groove is a full circle while the discs use only its top, so the empty lower half is visible. It can be cut to the arc.

options.label: B · tighter, with names
options.thesis: 148 degrees, a smaller disc, the hub pulled down - all to make room for the eight names the fan has been missing.
options.viewport: Eight discs, each with its word.
options.risk: DEFECT, and it settles the question: the names collide with the neighbouring discs. Eight Hebrew words do not fit on an arc this size at any setting I tried. Judge it as evidence, not as a proposal.

options.label: C · a full dial
options.thesis: Eight discs evenly around a complete ring. The one arrangement where the spacing is provably even and no disc is special, seated in the same pressed channel.
options.viewport: A closed ring around the hub.
options.risk: It is no longer a fan. It also puts an area at the very bottom of the screen, under the hub, which is the hardest place to reach with a thumb.
